solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cocktail skirt full of style

indicators.note: a thing that is full of something holds it inside, so one word's letters go within the other's

parts.note: a miniskirt, a mini for short
artistry or style, as in 'the art of conversation'

explanation.surface: A fashion note: a stylish skirt, perhaps worn to a cocktail party.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a classic cocktail of gin or vodka with vermouth, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: Gorgon alarmed us all, to some extent

indicators.note: only part of the following words is used, so the answer sits inside a stretch of them

parts.note: running across the end of the first word, the whole second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A monster frightened everyone a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Medusa is the most famous of the three Gorgons of Greek myth, whose gaze turned people to stone.

clue.text: Join again indeed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as ..., to form an alliance once more

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense needs the word split as re-ally, a prefix meaning again plus ally, to unite.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb it is a synonym of indeed; as a verb, split with a hyphen, it means to form a fresh alliance.

clue.text: Wrong home account by clergyman

parts.note: AC is the standard abbreviation for account
a curate is an assistant parish priest

explanation.surface: A vicar has misreported the household accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inaccurate is incorrect or mistaken, a plain synonym of wrong as an adjective.

clue.text: Trader's declaration is spot on

definitions.meaning: first meaning: read as ..., what a trader might say of themselves

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: a dealer announces 'I deal', which runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect or exactly as it should be, which is what the colloquial spot on conveys.

clue.text: Colin is building a semiconductor

indicators.note: building means constructing something new, so the given letters are assembled into a different shape

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A man called Colin is constructing an electronic component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' looks like a link to the definition, but it belongs to the fodder: Colin plus is supplies all seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicon is the chemical element most widely used as a semiconductor in computer chips.

clue.text: Special interest group starts environment subscription

parts.note: SIG is the usual abbreviation for a special interest group
nature, the natural world around us

explanation.surface: An enthusiasts' society launches a green membership scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts' simply places the group's letters at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscription in its older sense is a name written beneath a document, i.e. a signature.

clue.text: See 12
Grumble as corrupt policeman misses the last bit of evidence

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or perverted, so the letters are twisted out of their order
something that misses a thing goes without it, so that letter is taken out
the last bit of a word is its final letter only

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a bent officer has overlooked a key clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the E out of policeman, then rearrange the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To complain is to grumble or voice dissatisfaction, a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: French city connections showing elements of refinement

explanation.surface: Links with a French town display a cultured touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are fine points of etiquette or precision, the small details that mark polish and good manners.

clue.text: Doctor in the morning facing a crisis

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: A medic is confronted with an emergency first thing in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' tempts you to put one piece inside another, but here the pieces simply follow each other.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama, in everyday speech, is an exciting or troublesome incident, a fuss or crisis.

clue.text: So no recording device can be both practical and convenient

explanation.surface: A recording gadget that is useful and handy, then, would be no bad thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergonomic design suits the human user, so it is comfortable, efficient and easy to work with.

clue.text: Last resort vendor said to be one that stores seasoning

indicators.note: re-sort means sort again, so the letters are put into a fresh order
said means spoken, so the word is wanted for how it sounds

explanation.surface: A trader at a seaside town, the final holiday spot, keeps the condiments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last resort' reads as a set phrase, but resort is split off as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A salt cellar is a small dish or shaker that holds table salt, a seasoning.

clue.text: Story with us making lentil soup

indicators.note: the answer plus the extra word together make the phrase, rearranged
the answer only becomes the fodder when joined with another word, so that word must be stripped back out

parts.note: taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A tale about cooking a pulse-based broth together.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a compound anagram: answer plus US rearranges to LENTIL SOUP, so remove U and S from those letters and rearrange the eight left.
explanation.definitionFit: A plotline is the storyline of a novel, film or play, a near synonym of story.

clue.text: Cryptic clue by Goliath: old-fashioned or enlightened?

indicators.note: something cryptic is obscure or scrambled, so the following word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves is I

explanation.surface: The setter asks whether one of his clues is stale or illuminating.
explanation.walkthrough: Goliath is this puzzle's setter, so his name stands for the first person, I.
explanation.definitionFit: Elucidated means made clear or explained, so a matter elucidated has been enlightened or illuminated.

clue.text: Writer outwardly in tears managed to calm down

indicators.note: outwardly means on the outside, so the rearranged phrase wraps around the other word
managed means handled or arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a quill pen, an old writing implement

explanation.surface: An author in floods of tears managed to compose themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in tears' is not a position but fodder: its seven letters are shuffled and split around the writer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tranquillise is to make calm or sedate, as the transitive sense of calm down.

clue.text: Different age once, still endlessly harking back

indicators.note: different signals that the letters are made into a different arrangement

parts.note: endlessly tells us to drop the last letter of each of the three words age, once and still

explanation.surface: Someone muses that times were different back then, still looking fondly to the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims each of age, once and still, leaving AG, ONC and STIL; 'Different' then rearranges those nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostalgic person longs for the past, so their thoughts keep returning to earlier times.

clue.text: Settle with supermodel, as admitted

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould, so the word before it is reshaped
a word that is admitted is let in, so it goes inside the other letters

parts.note: split as super and model: the first five letters, reshaped as the second part instructs
qua is Latin for in the capacity of, i.e. as

explanation.surface: Someone pays their bill with a fashion model, who confessed as much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supermodel' must be split into super and model, the second word being the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To square up is to pay what is owed, i.e. to settle an account.

clue.text: Celery, if cooked with vigour

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are turned into something new

explanation.surface: A recipe note: celery, when cooked, should be stirred vigorously.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiercely means with intensity or energy, an adverb matching the adverbial phrase with vigour.

clue.text: Epitome of complex sentences to follow a French question

indicators.note: complex means complicated or tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Grammar talk: tangled sentences follow a question asked in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' tells you the anagram comes after the question word. The printed key misspells the answer with a C for the second S.
explanation.definitionFit: The quintessence of something is its purest or most perfect example, which is what an epitome is.

clue.text: Hostile lines

definitions.meaning: second meaning: read as ..., some lines of poetry

explanation.walkthrough: The second sense needs the answer split into two words: a verse is a set of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means being opposed or unfriendly towards it, a near synonym of hostile.

clue.text: Mate could be Dr Evil?

parts.note: a fiend is an evil being
the letter of Dr not already in the evil one

explanation.surface: Could the Austin Powers villain Dr Evil be somebody's pal?
explanation.walkthrough: A loose clue: a fiend with the R of Dr slipped in after its first letter becomes a mate; Dr Evil, the comic villain, is the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Mate is informal British and Australian English for a friend or pal.

clue.text: Wrong to be wary when leaders change

indicators.note: the leading letters swap places, a small rearrangement of the word's front

explanation.surface: It is a mistake to be cautious when the people in charge are replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' means the first two letters, which trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: Awry means amiss or off course, so things that have gone awry have gone wrong.

clue.text: Ignored antiquated port

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned harbour has been neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: To be passed over is to be overlooked or disregarded, e.g. for promotion, so it means ignored.

clue.text: Artist mostly playing this instrument

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are toyed with and rearranged
mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A musician performs, usually on this particular instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitar is a long-necked plucked string instrument of Indian classical music.

clue.text: Marble perhaps used in popular churches

indicators.note: the letters are used within the following words, sitting inside them

parts.note: across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Marble may be a building material in well-attended churches.
explanation.walkthrough: Marble looks like the stone, but it is Marble Arch, the London landmark, so 'perhaps' marks an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Marble Arch is a famous triumphal arch in London, an example of the structure.

clue.text: Military command making sense about the ides of March

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: sight, one of the five senses

indicators.note: the ides fall in the middle of a Roman month, so the middle letter of the month's name is wanted

parts.note: the central letter of the five

explanation.surface: A soldier's order is reminiscent of Caesar's warning about the ides of March.
explanation.walkthrough: The Roman ides fell around the middle of the month, here the middle of the word March.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes right is a parade-ground order telling troops to turn their heads to the right, e.g. in salute.

clue.text: Where to find inaccurate number

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the clue numbered ... down in this grid has inaccurate as its answer

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cross-reference: inaccurate is the answer at 3 in this very puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Three is a cardinal number, so it is an example of the general term.

clue.text: Clairvoyant is occasionally posey and elegant

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: A fortune teller is at times pretentious but stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: Posey, British slang, means pretentious or showing off.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychic claims powers of the mind such as clairvoyance, so the two are synonyms as nouns.

clue.text: Ginger Romeo?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person with red hair, as ginger is a nickname for one
second meaning: read as ..., the first letter of red, which Romeo stands for in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.walkthrough: Romeo is the NATO alphabet code word for R, and R is the head of the word red; the question mark flags this wordplay-style definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger is a British nickname for someone with red hair, which is what a redhead has.
